title: Which region is hiring fastest?
objective: Learners compare two years of monthly new hires across three regions and identify the fastest-growing region by its growth rate, not by its size.

recommended.why: A standard multi-line chart with a legend and tooltips is the quickest, most familiar way to compare three monthly series.

alternative.why: Standard configuration versus custom control: direct labels and an annotation versus a legend and a title.

assumptions: Hiring numbers are illustrative synthetic data from a seeded generator, not real company figures
Three regions with different sizes and underlying growth, plus a shared seasonal pattern (December dip, spring and autumn peaks)
Growth = hires in Jul–Dec 2025 divided by hires in Jul–Dec 2024, minus 1, computed on unsmoothed monthly counts
Smoothing is a trailing average; the months before Jan 2024 are generated so every shown month has a full window
Change vs same month last year = (this month ÷ same month a year earlier − 1), on the displayed series
units: change: percent vs the same month one year earlier
checkDescription: The highlighted region is the one with the highest growth (last 6 months vs the same months a year earlier); every smoothed month is its window mean, and smoothing never changes which region hires the most in total.

learnerPrompts.predict: Before playing: which region do you expect to be growing fastest, the biggest one or one of the smaller ones?
learnerPrompts.explain: Switch Show to 'Change vs last year'. Why does that view make the fastest-growing region obvious when the monthly view does not?
